For a finite-dimensional integrable vector law, its mean lies in the closed convex hull by separation. If the mean is not relatively interior, use a supporting hyperplane in the affine span. A nonnegative signed distance has expectation zero, so the response law is supported on that hyperplane. Iteration strictly lowers dimension until relative interior membership yields membership in the actual convex hull.

Planar Carathéodory gives at most three actual caps with probability weights preserving zero response. One weight is at least 1/3. The strict positive-margin hinge is convex and its positive support is fully paid by that cap.

When the through-mark cap only supports its own fiber, adding a positive shift gives a positive boundary integral at a boundary maximizer. The selected ramp pays at least 1-eta/H on this field's support. Taking the supremum and eta down to zero gives the same bound. For pure-base caps use the finite set of negative base margin gaps to make support exactly fully captured.

The guard family has balanced active menus and its upper bound tends to 1/3 with unbounded integer dimension. This yields a universal infimum, with no claim that a finite guard member attains that infimum.
